heading: Frontend Build Recovery
text: After renaming a transfer object, container or page, the generated names derived from it change: customization component names and interface keys (`<ContainerComponentName>...Component`, upper-snake `..._INTERFACE_KEY`), page and dialog folders. Rename the matching custom files and constants by hand, delete the stale generated `src/pages/`, `src/dialog/`, `src/containers/` and `src/services/` folders, then run `./judo.sh build -i`.

heading: Starting Services
text: `./judo.sh start` needs a running Docker daemon: it starts the PostgreSQL and Keycloak containers (or the Compose stack). Run `docker info` first; if it fails, start Docker before `start`. The command launches Karaf in the background (console output in `application/.karaf/console.out`) and returns before the application is ready, so wait for the application URL to answer with HTTP 200 before running tests; connection-refused errors in tests usually mean the stack is not up yet.
evidence: judo-esm-fullstack-project-template/judo-esm-fullstack-project-template-root/src/main/resources/judo.sh.hbs:471 (docker containers), :622-635 (Karaf background start, console.out). judo.sh has no Docker daemon check or readiness wait that could be confirmed from the digests (judo.sh.hbs not in wt).

heading: Troubleshooting
text:
### `Unable to access jarfile` for `target/judo-cli.jar`

`target/judo-cli.jar` is copied into the root `target/` only by a `generate-root` run (the download execution overwrites it each time); a plain `mvn install` does not produce it. If the jar is missing (after a clean, a prune or a fresh checkout), run `./judo.sh generate-root` to restore it before calling the CLI.
evidence: judo-esm-fullstack-project-template/.../pom.xml.hbs:513,531,541; openspec change root-only-cli-download. Cause of a specific disappearance is not established: `generate`/`generate-root` run `mvnd clean compile` (judo.sh.hbs:1111) and `prune` runs git clean (judo.sh.hbs:379).

heading: Deploying a Model as an OSGi Bundle
text:
### Libraries already in the runtime

The generated `<app>-judo-platform-prototype` Karaf feature already contains Tika (`tika-core`, `tika-parsers` 1.28.5) and PDFBox 2.0.13, and the OSGi e-mail feature brings Handlebars 4.2.0. Reuse them for document or template rendering instead of adding new bundles; add a bundle only for a library that is not listed here. (Reconcile best-practices `osgi-karaf-bundle-architecture.md`: its line 'Extra third-party bundles (Tika, PDFBox, CXF, Handlebars, JODConverter) are added to the Karaf feature' should read 'Extra third-party bundles not already in the runtime (for example JODConverter) are added to the Karaf feature'. Verify that the e-mail feature is installed in the target runtime before relying on Handlebars.)

heading: Deploying a Model as an OSGi Bundle
text: Declarative Services components can be unit-tested without a container with `MockOsgi` from `osgi-utils` (`osgi-test`): `MockOsgi.activate`/`deactivate` call the `@Activate`/`@Deactivate` methods (parameters: none, `BundleContext`, `ComponentContext`, `Map`/`Dictionary`) and `MockOsgi.setReferences` injects services into `@Reference` fields or bind methods (Felix SCR and standard OSGi DS annotations).

heading: Element not found with getByRole/getByLabel
text: Generated pages can contain several elements with the same accessible name (for example a column menu button and the input of the same field), so `getByLabel('<Field>')` may match more than one element. Prefer the generated element ids: every generated visual element carries `data-testid` equal to its id (exported by the generated `VisualElementIds.ts`), and dropdown menu items use their id as `data-testid`. Otherwise narrow the lookup, for example `getByRole('textbox', { name })` or a scope inside `getByRole('dialog')`.
evidence: judo-ui-react-template/.../containers/container.tsx.hbs:93, components/DropdownButton.tsx.hbs; judo-ui-e2e-template openspec expand-e2e-visual-element-ids (VisualElementIds.ts, data-testid). The view-save button label 'Update' was not confirmed in source.

heading: Operation Issues
text:
### Action not visible in an action group

An action group shows only its first `featuredActions` actions as buttons; the remaining actions are inside a dropdown button with `data-testid` `<XMIID>-button-group`. Open the dropdown first, then click the menu item (menu items carry their own id as `data-testid`). The featured count is a model property of the action group.

heading: Environment Issues
text:
### `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED` in a long test

An expired Keycloak access token makes the backend answer HTTP 401 with code `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. The token lifetime is a Keycloak realm setting (access token lifespan), so a single long test (many steps, screenshots at several widths) can outlive it. Keep each test shorter than the lifespan or split it into tests that each log in.
evidence: judo-runtime-core KeycloakLoginInterceptor (TokenNotActiveException -> AuthenticationRequiredException code ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED); documentation developer-guide/03_error_codes.adoc:175. Realm lifespan value not found in source.

heading: Practice notes: seed through DAOs, guard against repeats
text: For a running-app (Playwright) test the DAO-based initializer is not a test hook. Seed state in the database instead: `./judo.sh dump` and `./judo.sh import` manage PostgreSQL dumps, so build a base dump once, and derive test data from it. Values that the application sets itself (for example creation timestamps) cannot be set through the generated REST API; backdate them with SQL against the PostgreSQL container, or leave that rule untested.
evidence: judo-esm-fullstack-project-template judo.sh commands dump/import (judo-tatami-jsl-tests digest, judo.sh.hbs:7). That timestamps cannot be set through the API is not confirmed in source (verify).

heading: Platform: realms come from the model
text: The realm JSON exported from the model contains only `id`, `realm`, `enabled`, `loginWithEmailAllowed` and the clients. It does not set `registrationAllowed`, so Keycloak's default (self sign-up off) applies and the login page hides the registration link. There is no model setting for it; enable self sign-up through the Keycloak admin API (`registrationAllowed=true` on the realm) or in the realm configuration after import.
evidence: judo-meta-keycloak/model/src/main/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/meta/keycloak/runtime/exporter/Keycloak... (exported keys exactly id, realm, enabled, loginWithEmailAllowed, clients); judo-keycloak login.ftl (registration link only when realm.registrationAllowed); only the project template's test-users-realm.json sets registrationAllowed=true.

Platform facts available: PDFBox 2.0.13 (generated feature.xml.hbs:20) and Handlebars 4.2.0 (osgi-email feature.xml:34) ship in the runtime; FileStoreService returns file ids. The Markdown-to-PDF step is project code with no platform source; a recipe page needs an author decision (see G133 text for the library facts).

heading: Practice
text: Treat the filter as a read-side restriction and verify direct access by identifier: a signed identifier is a JWS with subject = identifier and claims entity type, version and issuer (the reference or operation that produced it); it carries no user or actor claim, and verification only checks that the type matches. Do not assume that opening another actor's record by its page address is refused. *Verify* with the dispatcher, and enforce ownership in the model or in a write/read guard (interceptor or checks inside custom operations).
evidence: judo-runtime-core/judo-runtime-core-dispatcher/.../DefaultIdentifierSigner.java (claims, hasCorrectSigner -> ACCESS_DENIED_INVALID_TYPE). Whether a direct GET/update by identifier applies the derived access filter was not found in source.

heading: Variations
text: - **Invitee must be a Keycloak user**: the generated realm leaves self sign-up off (see `multi-tenant-keycloak-realm`), so an anonymous actor cannot accept the key without an account. Enable self sign-up on the realm, let the invitee register first, then accept the key as the signed-in actor.
evidence: judo-meta-keycloak exporter (no registrationAllowed in generated realm); same evidence as G112. Choosing sign-up-first over anonymous acceptance remains a design decision.

No scheduler or Quartz feature appears in the judo-platform, karaf-features or template digests (only an internal thread-pool scheduler in judo-tatami-core). Absence in digests does not prove the runtime has none; the app-defined scheduler bundle approach is a project route. Not settled.

heading: Know the limits of the aggregates
text: Only `!count()` is wrapped to return 0 on an empty collection (`COALESCE(..., 0)`); `!sum`, `!avg`, `!min` and `!max` are plain aggregates over a sub-select, so on an empty collection they return no value (undefined) without an error. Check `!count()` (or `!isDefined()`) before using the result in a label. Integer collections do not support `!avg` (only sum, min and max).
evidence: judo-runtime-core-dao-rdbms SubSelectFeatureMapper (COUNT -> COALESCE({0}.{1}, 0)); DecimalAggregatedExpressionToFeatureConverter.java:67; IntegerAggregatedExpressionToFeatureConverter (no AVG). Empty-collection NULL result for non-count aggregates inferred from the absence of COALESCE; verify at runtime.
